prompt:
Flat sumi-e ink wash painting on aged warm paper. Hand-painted, not rendered. A single isolated subject on plain paper, centred, whole subject in frame. Dark tapering brush outline, flat even ink-wash fill, uniform ambient tone with no visible light source, no cast shadow, no sheen. Monochromatic warm grey from pale paper to near-black ink. Brush character at every edge.

Subject: one gnarled old Japanese cliff pine drawn as an isometric game asset, viewed from a high three-quarter angle (looking down at about 45 degrees), so it reads as a solid object with depth. A chunky grey rock base, roughly round, seen from above so its top face shows. From it rises a very thick, stout, twisted near-black trunk that leans and bends in crooked elbows. Five thick branches radiate outward in all directions around the trunk like spokes: two toward the viewer, two away, one to the side. Each branch ends in one thick round flat-topped cushion of dark needle foliage, drawn as a fat disc whose round top face is fully visible from above, like a lily pad with thickness. The cushions are spread around the trunk at different heights and depths, the nearer ones overlapping the farther ones. Thick, heavy, simple forms: no thin twigs, no loose needles, no wispy strokes. Only warm greys and near-black: no brown, no green.

Plain empty paper background and nothing else in the picture: no ground line, no cliff wall, no mist, no clouds, no shadow, no text, no seal. Whole subject in frame with a paper margin all round.
